findings.summary: Sample check R1: The plan states the subsystem must accept exactly one plan_package_final.json plus an associated structured handoff bundle as the sole canonical planning input, but the intake/tool-policy and interface contracts shown only operationalize plan_package_final.json (and other context artifacts) and do not specify how the structured handoff bundle is represented/validated, nor how “exactly one” is deterministically enforced/rejected for non-canonical inputs.

evidence.note: R1 includes “exactly one frozen plan_package_final.json (plus its associated structured handoff bundle)” and rejection of chat logs/non-canonical artifacts.
High-level dataflow lists inputs as plan_package_final.json + repo_context.json + workspace_context.json; does not mention a structured handoff bundle contract/validation.

Intake HITL triggers list missing required inputs including plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json; does not list the structured handoff bundle as a required validated input.

findings.summary: Sample check R2: repo_context.json is required and described at a high level, but the candidate does not provide (within the sampled material) a concrete typed/versioned schema definition or resolved constraints for protected/forbidden paths; open questions indicate the repo_context schema and forbidden/protected paths enforcement details remain blocking, which undermines the “schema-invalid → fail before code-gen” requirement.

evidence.note: R2 requires a typed/versioned repo_context.json schema with specific minimum fields and validator behavior.
Q4 is blocking: forbidden/protected paths patterns and what constitutes high-risk operations are not yet defined.
Q14 is blocking: required schema for repo_context.json protected/forbidden paths and enforcement details are explicitly unresolved.
M1 deliverable claims validated repo_context.json with schema-pass confirmation, but the actual schema artifact/spec is not present in the sampled content.

findings.summary: Sample check R3: workspace_context.json is required and described at a high level, but the candidate does not provide (within the sampled material) a concrete typed/versioned schema definition and leaves key workspace backend and context-pack bounding constraints as blocking open questions; this weakens the determinism of “schema-invalid → fail before workspace-writing stage.”

evidence.note: R3 requires a typed/versioned workspace_context.json schema with minimum fields and validator behavior.
Q2 is blocking: permitted workspace backends and hard constraints are unresolved.
Q15 is blocking: context-pack bounding/selection when workspace grows beyond context windows is unresolved (directly tied to workspace_context rules).
O2 relies on a Workspace Manager with namespaced partitions and unified workspace_index, implying workspace_context must specify partition/layout rules; concrete schema not shown in sampled content.
